questions.questionText: The force on charge q moving with velocity v in magnetic field B is:
questions.solution: Lorentz force F = q(v x B), a cross product.

questions.questionText: A charged particle moving parallel to B experiences:
questions.solution: F = qvB sin(theta). theta=0 gives F=0.

questions.questionText: Magnetic field at centre of a circular coil of radius R carrying current I is:
questions.solution: Biot-Savart law gives B = mu0*I/(2R) at centre.

questions.questionText: In a cyclotron the frequency of revolution:
questions.solution: f = qB/(2*pi*m), independent of speed and radius.

questions.questionText: Two parallel wires with currents in the same direction:
questions.solution: Parallel currents in same direction attract.

questions.questionText: Magnetic field inside a long solenoid is:
questions.solution: B = mu0*n*I inside solenoid.

questions.questionText: Torque on a current loop of moment M in field B is:
questions.solution: Torque = M x B (cross product).

questions.solution: Magnetic force provides centripetal force making a circle.

questions.questionText: Force on a current-carrying conductor of length L at angle theta to B is:
questions.solution: F = BIL sin(theta).

questions.questionText: Biot-Savart law is analogous to:
questions.solution: Both give field due to a source element (charge or current).

questions.questionText: Magnetic field on axis of current loop at large distance varies as:
questions.solution: At large distance loop acts as dipole: field falls as 1/r^3.

questions.questionText: Magnetic moment of a current loop of area A with current I is:
questions.solution: m = NIA. For single loop m = IA.

questions.questionText: Ampere's circuital law states:
questions.optionA: Line integral of B around closed loop = mu0*I_enclosed
questions.optionB: Line integral of E around closed loop = 0
questions.solution: Ampere's law: integral B.dl = mu0*I_enclosed.

questions.questionText: Radius of circular path of charge q, mass m, velocity v in field B is:
questions.solution: qvB = mv^2/r gives r = mv/(qB).

questions.questionText: A toroid is essentially:
questions.optionB: A solenoid bent into a ring
questions.solution: Toroid is a solenoid bent into a closed ring.

questions.questionText: Magnetic field outside a toroid is:
questions.solution: Field outside an ideal toroid is zero.

questions.questionText: Galvanometer sensitivity increases by:
questions.solution: Sensitivity proportional to NBA/k. Larger A increases it.
